Controlled evidence exists, but does not establish a NextItNet-specific winner. [Di Teodoro et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.07770) compare BCE, BPR and categorical cross-entropy across five datasets/four models; importantly, candidate CE with exactly one negative equals BPR: log(1+exp(s_negative−s_positive)). [Wu et al.](https://wujcan.github.io/papers/tois-ssm.pdf) separately ablate negative count, sampling distribution and in-batch sampling, including multiple-negative BCE/BPR controls. Their recommendation results are useful evidence, not guaranteed NextItNet outcomes.

Uncorrected candidate CE, −log[exp(s_positive)/(exp(s_positive)+Σexp(s_negative))], learns discrimination within sampled candidates. Increasing negatives changes its competition and gradient weighting. Averaged BPR instead estimates the same expected pairwise loss as negative count increases; summed BPR additionally changes scale. BCE independently classifies positives/negatives, so averaging all terms versus separately averaging positive and negative terms changes class weighting. Sampling-corrected softmax uses proposal/expected-count corrections to approximate a specified full-softmax objective; finite-sample gradients generally remain biased. A constant correction applied to every candidate cancels, while treating the guaranteed positive separately can matter. See [Blanc and Rendle](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v80/blanc18a.html) and [Khrylchenko et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331).

Design implication: uniform sampling without replacement removes duplicate weighting; for K negatives from M eligible items, inclusion probability is K/M. Excluding every user training positive prevents known-positive collisions but changes support to user-specific unseen items; it cannot estimate an unrestricted catalog denominator without restoring excluded contributions. Unobserved items can still be relevant. These are mathematical implications, not demonstrated NextItNet gains. Run a factorial control: fixed NextItNet backbone/data/updates, loss × negative count, identical eligible pools and sampled candidates across losses; then separately toggle replacement, positive exclusion and correction. Report loss reductions explicitly and retain pinned macro validation HR@10.
